# 1 Samuel Chapter 1 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 131r–131v | **Source Image:** 1SA_001_page_001.jpg, 1SA_001_page_002.jpg

---

**1:1** There was a certain man from Ramathaim-zophim, from the hill country of Ephraim, and his name was Elkanah the son of Jeroham, the son of Elihu, the son of Tohu, the son of Zuph, an Ephrathite.

**1:2** And he had two wives; the name of the one was Hannah, and the name of the second was Peninnah. And Peninnah had children, but Hannah had no children.

**1:3** And this man would go up from his city year by year to worship and to sacrifice to the LORD of Hosts at Shiloh. And the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were priests of the LORD there.

**1:4** And on the day when Elkanah sacrificed, he would give portions to Peninnah his wife and to all her sons and her daughters.

**1:5** But to Hannah he would give a double portion, because he loved Hannah, though the LORD had closed her womb.

**1:6** And her rival would provoke her bitterly, so as to irritate her, because the LORD had closed her womb.

**1:7** And so it was year by year; as often as she went up to the house of the LORD, her rival would provoke her. And she wept and would not eat.

**1:8** And Elkanah her husband said to her, "Hannah, why do you weep? And why do you not eat? And why is your heart grieved? Am I not better to you than ten sons?"

**1:9** And Hannah rose after eating and after drinking in Shiloh. Now Eli the priest was sitting upon his seat by the doorpost of the temple of the LORD.

**1:10** And she was bitter of soul, and she prayed to the LORD, weeping bitterly.

**1:11** And she vowed a vow and said, "O LORD of Hosts, if you will indeed look upon the affliction of your maidservant, and remember me, and not forget your maidservant, but will give to your maidservant a son, then I will give him to the LORD all the days of his life, and no razor shall come upon his head."

**1:12** And it came to pass, as she continued praying before the LORD, that Eli watched her mouth.

**1:13** Now Hannah was speaking in her heart; only her lips moved, but her voice was not heard. And Eli took her to be drunk.

**1:14** And Eli said to her, "How long will you be drunk? Put away your wine from you."

**1:15** And Hannah answered and said, "No, my lord, I am a woman hard-pressed in spirit. I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink, but I have been pouring out my soul before the LORD.

**1:16** Do not regard your maidservant as a worthless woman, for out of the abundance of my grief and my vexation I have spoken until now."

**1:17** And Eli answered and said, "Go in peace, and may the God of Israel grant your petition that you have asked of him."

**1:18** And she said, "May your maidservant find favor in your eyes." And the woman went her way and ate, and her face was no longer downcast.

**1:19** And they rose early in the morning and worshipped before the LORD, and they returned and came to their house in Ramah. And Elkanah knew Hannah his wife, and the LORD remembered her.

**1:20** And it came to pass at the turn of days that Hannah conceived and bore a son, and she called his name Samuel, saying, "Because I asked him of the LORD."

**1:21** And the man Elkanah went up with all his household to offer to the LORD the yearly sacrifice and his vow.

**1:22** But Hannah did not go up, for she said to her husband, "Not until the child is weaned; then I will bring him, that he may appear before the LORD and remain there forever."

**1:23** And Elkanah her husband said to her, "Do what is good in your eyes. Remain until you have weaned him; only may the LORD establish his word." So the woman remained and nursed her son until she weaned him.

**1:24** And she brought him up with her when she had weaned him, with three bulls and one ephah of flour and a skin of wine, and she brought him to the house of the LORD at Shiloh. And the child was young.

**1:25** And they slaughtered the bull, and they brought the child to Eli.

**1:26** And she said, "O my lord! As your soul lives, my lord, I am the woman who stood here beside you, praying to the LORD.

**1:27** For this child I prayed, and the LORD has granted me my petition that I asked of him.

**1:28** And I also have lent him to the LORD; all the days that he lives, he is lent to the LORD." And he worshipped the LORD there.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

All three translators agreed in substance on the following points:
- The genealogical introduction of Elkanah (v. 1) and the basic family situation (v. 2) were rendered consistently across all three.
- The annual pilgrimage to Shiloh (v. 3) and the sacrificial meal context (v. 4) were in full agreement.
- Hannah's silent prayer and Eli's misidentification of her as drunk (vv. 12-14) were uniformly rendered.
- Eli's blessing and Hannah's response (vv. 17-18) carried the same sense in all three versions.
- The naming of Samuel with the wordplay on "asked" (v. 20) was preserved by all translators.
- Hannah's dedication of Samuel to the LORD (vv. 26-28) was substantively identical across versions.

---
## ⚠️ Disagreement Log

**Verse 1 — "Ephrathite" vs. "Ephraimite":**
- EMET: "an Ephrathite" (literal from the Hebrew)
- LOGOS: "an Ephrathite"
- PNEUMA: "an Ephraimite"
- **SOPHIA resolution:** Retained "Ephrathite" following the MT reading. PNEUMA's "Ephraimite" is an interpretive modernization; the Hebrew text reads אֶפְרָתִי.

**Verse 5 — "a portion one of the face" vs. "double portion":**
- EMET: "a portion one of the face" (hyper-literal, with gloss "double portion")
- LOGOS: "a double portion"
- PNEUMA: "a double portion"
- **SOPHIA resolution:** Adopted "a double portion" as the consensus reading. The Hebrew is notoriously difficult, but the traditional understanding is well-supported and readable.

**Verse 6 — "make her thunder" vs. "make her fret" vs. "taunting her":**
- EMET: "to make her thunder" (literal rendering of רעם)
- LOGOS: "to make her fret"
- PNEUMA: "taunting her" / "provoke her relentlessly"
- **SOPHIA resolution:** Used "to irritate her," which captures the sense of persistent agitation without the opacity of "thunder" or the looseness of "taunting."

**Verse 7 — Subject of provocation:**
- EMET: "so she provoked her" (ambiguous subject)
- LOGOS: "so she would provoke her"
- PNEUMA: "Peninnah would needle her"
- **SOPHIA resolution:** Clarified with "her rival would provoke her," making the subject explicit without adding a name not in the Hebrew.

**Verse 8 — "is it evil to your heart" vs. "is your heart grieved" vs. "are you so downhearted":**
- EMET: "why is it evil to your heart?" (literal)
- LOGOS: "why is your heart grieved?"
- PNEUMA: "Why are you so downhearted?"
- **SOPHIA resolution:** Adopted LOGOS's "why is your heart grieved?" as a formal rendering that preserves the Hebrew idiom while being natural English.

**Verse 10 — "bitter of soul" vs. "in deep anguish":**
- EMET: "bitter of soul"
- LOGOS: "bitter of soul"
- PNEUMA: "In deep anguish"
- **SOPHIA resolution:** Retained "bitter of soul" (2-to-1 agreement, and it preserves the Hebrew nefesh idiom). Added "weeping bitterly" from LOGOS/PNEUMA for the second clause.

**Verse 11 — "a seed of men" vs. "a son":**
- EMET: "a seed of men" (literal Hebrew)
- LOGOS: "a son"
- PNEUMA: "a son"
- **SOPHIA resolution:** Adopted "a son" for clarity. The Hebrew idiom "seed of men" means a male child, and "a son" conveys this without ambiguity.

**Verse 11 — "if looking you will look" vs. "if you will indeed look" vs. "if you would only look — truly look":**
- EMET: "if looking you will look" (infinitive absolute construction)
- LOGOS: "if you will indeed look"
- PNEUMA: "if you would only look — truly look"
- **SOPHIA resolution:** Adopted LOGOS's "if you will indeed look" as formally accurate to the emphatic construction without the visual disruption of PNEUMA's dashes.

**Verse 13 — "thought her for a drunkard" vs. "thought her to be drunk" vs. "thought she was drunk":**
- EMET: "thought her for a drunkard"
- LOGOS: "thought her to be drunk"
- PNEUMA: "thought she was drunk"
- **SOPHIA resolution:** Used "took her to be drunk" — formal but natural, avoiding the archaic "drunkard."

**Verse 15 — "hard of spirit" vs. "hard-pressed in spirit" vs. "crushed in spirit":**
- EMET: "hard of spirit"
- LOGOS: "hard-pressed in spirit"
- PNEUMA: "crushed in spirit"
- **SOPHIA resolution:** Adopted "hard-pressed in spirit" from LOGOS. It conveys the weight of the Hebrew without over-translating ("crushed") or being too terse ("hard of").

**Verse 16 — "daughter of worthlessness" vs. "worthless woman":**
- EMET: "daughter of worthlessness [beliyyaal]"
- LOGOS: "a worthless woman"
- PNEUMA: "some worthless woman"
- **SOPHIA resolution:** Used "a worthless woman" with LOGOS and PNEUMA. The literal "daughter of beliyyaal" is too opaque for a consensus text.

**Verse 16 — "complaint and provocation" vs. "anxiety and vexation" vs. "grief and anguish":**
- EMET: "my complaint and my provocation"
- LOGOS: "my anxiety and my vexation"
- PNEUMA: "my grief and anguish"
- **SOPHIA resolution:** Used "my grief and my vexation" — combining PNEUMA's superior first term with LOGOS's more precise second term.

**Verse 18 — "her face was not to her still" vs. "no longer sad" vs. "no longer downcast":**
- EMET: "her face was not to her still" (hyper-literal)
- LOGOS: "her face was no longer sad"
- PNEUMA: "her face was no longer downcast"
- **SOPHIA resolution:** Adopted "her face was no longer downcast" from PNEUMA, which better captures the Hebrew idiom of facial expression changing.

**Verse 19 — "knew" vs. "was intimate with":**
- EMET: "knew"
- LOGOS: "knew"
- PNEUMA: "was intimate with"
- **SOPHIA resolution:** Retained "knew" (2-to-1 agreement; the biblical idiom is well-understood).

**Verse 20 — "at the circuit of the days" vs. "at the turn of days" vs. "in the course of time":**
- EMET: "at the circuit of the days"
- LOGOS: "at the turn of days"
- PNEUMA: "In the course of time"
- **SOPHIA resolution:** Adopted LOGOS's "at the turn of days," which is formally precise while still readable.

**Verse 22 — "until forever" vs. "forever" vs. "permanently":**
- EMET: "until forever"
- LOGOS: "forever"
- PNEUMA: "permanently"
- **SOPHIA resolution:** Used "forever" as the standard English rendering of the Hebrew.

**Verse 24 — "with bulls three" vs. "with three bulls" vs. "a three-year-old bull":**
- EMET: "with bulls three" (MT plural reading)
- LOGOS: "with three bulls" (MT reading, natural English order)
- PNEUMA: "a three-year-old bull" (following LXX/4QSam-a)
- **SOPHIA resolution:** Followed the MT with LOGOS's "with three bulls." PNEUMA follows the LXX variant, but SOPHIA defaults to the Leningrad Codex as the source text.

**Verse 24 — "the lad was a lad" vs. "the child was young" vs. "the boy was still young":**
- EMET: "the lad was a lad" (hyper-literal)
- LOGOS: "the child was young"
- PNEUMA: "The boy was still young"
- **SOPHIA resolution:** Used "the child was young" from LOGOS — clear and dignified.

**Verse 28 — "lent him to the LORD" vs. "giving him to the LORD":**
- EMET: "I have lent him to the LORD"
- LOGOS: "I also have lent him to the LORD"
- PNEUMA: "I am giving him to the LORD"
- **SOPHIA resolution:** Retained "lent" (EMET/LOGOS) to preserve the crucial wordplay with sha'al (ask/lend), which threads through the chapter.
